newsitem.title: GERMANY: German building union accepts minimum wage deal.
newsitem.headline: German building union accepts minimum wage deal.

text.p: German construction trade union IG Bau said on Monday it had accepted employers' proposals of a generally-binding minimum wage for the industry that would be valid until August 31, 1997.
The agreement follows the failure of attempts earlier this year by IG Bau and industry associations to set a minimum wage for workers in the sector.

A spokesman for IG Bau confirmed the minimum wage will be set at 17 marks for west German workers and 15.64 for those in the east -- still some way down on the 18.60 marks and 17.11 marks respectively it had orginally sought.
"The employers have however now moved a bit further forwards," IG Bau chairman Klaus Wiesehuegel said in a statement. Employers had originally set a May 31 deadline on any minimum wage agreement.
Wiesehuegel said it would now be possible to test minimum wages, and a related ruling that foreign-owned contractors also observe minimum wages, during part of the peak of the building season.

A previous wage agreement foundered in April after the BDA -- the umbrella employers' federation for the industry -- vetoed it, saying it exceeded lowest wages in other sectors and carried an inflationary risk.
